army.$comment: Commander aura, supply cart and watchman (D69).

watchman.$comment: PK: the hunter-scout walks with his dog to find stone, gold, gems and fruit; when he sees a source he goes back to tell the king (reportAtM in front of the hall). On the way he and the dog take game they meet within huntTiles; the kill is meat for the villagers. He keeps the hides of what he kills (hideShare of the meat, in gold) and sells them at a store when he has hidesCap or more, or when he reports to the king; hides as trade goods are a gameplay abstraction. Hidden places (Kbal Spean, Mahendraparvata, Beng Mealea, Banteay Chhmar) are not marked on the map until found; the hunter heads for one within seekPlacesTiles.

livestock.$comment: Village animals round houses and fields (PK, D70); decoration only.

produce.$comment: Hay Day-style collecting (PK): the chickens and pigs at houses and the hall fill a basket (eggs, a piglet's worth) every everySec; click the basket over the house to take the food. On a live stream nobody may click, so it is taken in by itself autoSec later.

court.$comment: PK: the king is active and happy when the city grows. A finished building or new people make him bless the city (arms raised, the Brahmins with him), at most once per blessEverySec; every milestone people a toast says so.

orders.$comment: Hay Day-style order board (PK: features like Hay Day). Buyers ask for a few of the kingdom's goods and pay in gold; a filled or thrown-away slot gets a new buyer after a wait. Now and then a Chinese junk comes up the river with a big order and leaves if it is not filled. Zhou Daguan (1296): Chinese merchants traded at Angkor and the women kept the market; the buyers and amounts here are gameplay.

rice.$comment: The rice year in a field (PK, history first): the farmer sows the seed on a seedling bed (ព្រោះស្រូវ), brings water in with the rahat, a treadle water wheel still used in Cambodia (ដាក់ទឹកស្រែ ដោយរហាត់ទឹក), transplants the seedlings into rows (ស្ទូងស្រូវ), tends the rice and reaps it with a sickle (ច្រូតស្រូវ). Seedbed and transplanting are the traditional Khmer way; Zhou Daguan (1296) writes that fields gave three or four harvests a year. The rahat is known from later centuries (no Angkor-period depiction): HISTORICALLY_UNCERTAIN. The year moves on while a farmer works the field (cycleSec of work); the harvest brings in harvestFood more on top of the food gathered as before. Times are gameplay.

rafts.$comment: PK: people cross rivers, moats and the lake on boats or bamboo rafts (ក្បូនឬស្សី) instead of walking round. Boats on the Tonle Sap (fishing boats, the naval battle) are carved on the Bayon; Zhou Daguan describes boats of planks and dug-out canoes. Rafts for one person are a game abstraction. A water tile costs `cost` times a land tile when paths are planned; people move at `speed` of their walking pace on it.

alerts.$comment: PK: light alerts. A soft blue light over work in progress (building, training, research), a gold flash when it is finished, a red pulse on a resource that is running out (below lowRes) and on what a build or order still needs, an amber light over a lumber camp holding campFull timber or more (waiting for a cart).

decree.$comment: PK: the king's decree to build the temple. Every everySec seconds the villagers are set to work: before the foundation they gather what the temple still lacks (in proportion), then the foundation is laid on the temple's site and up to maxBuilders build it; farmers stay on their fields when keepFarmers. It ends when the temple stands.

ceremonies.$comment: PK: the king holds religious ceremonies by himself to build his royal power (ព្រះបារមី). One comes every everySec game seconds, the next of those allowed in the era; while it lasts (durSec) the people gather and build faster (buff), and the royal power grows. The ceremonies are taken from the record: the devaraja rite of 802 (Sdok Kok Thom inscription), royal consecration by the purohita and the consecration of a temple's image (inscriptions), and the yearly festivals Zhou Daguan saw at Angkor in 1296–97. Effects are gameplay. Zhou Daguan saw his festivals in 1296–97; showing them in earlier eras is likely but not attested.
